title: Judge Orders New York to Scrap Rollout of Second-Home Tax and Start Over
partialText: A Staten Island judge sided with a group of homeowners who had sued the city over its introduction of the tax, dealing a blow to Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

title: Supreme Court Allows Rapid Third-Country Deportations, for Now
partialText: The court also announced it would hear arguments in December on the legality of the Trump administration policy to swiftly deport immigrants to countries not their own.

title: ICE Plans 5,000 New Hires to Help With Deportation Drive
partialText: A similar surge last year resulted in undervetted officers initially being let in and then removed as the agency skipped basic checks for new recruits.

title: Man Shot by ICE Agent in Austin Is Charged With Assault
partialText: Prosecutors say Wilber Garces Perez struck an agent with his car’s mirror before another agent shot him. The charge reveals the existence of body camera footage of the shooting, though that video has not been released.

title: Trump Administration Prepares to Ask Tax Filers if They Are U.S. Citizens
partialText: The new question, included on a draft version of the primary tax form, comes as part of an anti-immigrant turn at an agency that long prioritized tax administration.

title: OpenAI Ignored Employees’ Warnings About Safely Testing A.I. Models
partialText: Employees and security researchers said that they had cautioned the company on safely testing its A.I. models and strengthening its corporate infrastructure, but that OpenAI did not listen.

title: OpenAI Apologizes for Australia Medicare Hack
partialText: The company detailed how A.I. agents gained access to four government websites and acknowledged mishandling its response.

title: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
partialText: Dorm Room Fund, a program that lets college students invest in their peers, raised a new $50 million fund as the competition for young founders ramps up.

title: Victor Marx, Colorado Governor Nominee With Sensational Past, Splinters the G.O.P.
partialText: Some Republicans in the state fear that the sensational biography of Victor Marx, their party’s candidate for governor, could drag down the rest of the ticket.

title: His Jet vs. Her Jeep: How Wealth Is Playing in the Midterms
partialText: In the so-called affordability election, two candidates for governor of Ohio are sparring over whether billionaires are the problem or the solution.

title: Cornell University Rape Investigation: What We Know
partialText: Prosecutors have reopened the case of a woman who said she was sexually assaulted on campus in 2024. The woman’s lawsuit brought renewed pressure to reopen the investigation.

title: Is Claude Conscious? Inside Anthropic’s Quest to Instill Morality Into Its A.I. Models
partialText: In a series of private meetings, the company consulted religious scholars to help instill morality into its A.I. models — and make the case that Claude could be conscious.

title: Ukrainian Science Academy, Struck by Drone, Played Key Role in Research
partialText: Over 90 percent of Ukraine’s scientific discoveries have been attributed to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences, including advancements in astronomy and military technology.

title: What Life Looks Like in the ‘Fortress Cities’ Russia Is Trying to Break
partialText: Emergency workers have to move fast after Russian attacks in eastern Ukraine. Another could come at any moment.

title: Trump Has Become Just Another Disappointing Politician
partialText: His winning brand — outsider businessman — has withered.

title: Trump’s Luck Is Finally Running Out
partialText: Voters are showing a growing determination to repudiate his presidency.

title: MacArthur Foundation Announces 2026 ‘Genius Grant’ Winners
partialText: The 20 fellowship recipients across the arts, humanities and sciences will each receive an $800,000, no-strings-attached stipend for their work.
